title: Magnetothermopower and particle-hole symmetry in a cuprate strange metal
authors: Yu-Te Hsu, Matija Čulo, Thom Ottenbros, Yingkai Huang, Jake Ayres, Steffen Wiedmann, Mikhail I. Katsnelson, Nigel E. Hussey, Mikhail Titov
abstract: Here, we report magnetothermopower measurements on overdoped (Bi,Pb)2(Sr,La)2CuO6+delta (Bi2201) single crystals in magnetic fields up to 35 T. Whereas the temperature dependence of the zero-field Seebeck coefficient S(T) can be captured using Boltzmann transport theory, the field-dependent response S(H) cannot. Instead, the magnetothermopower contains a large additional contribution whose field and temperature dependence is consistent with the presence of short-range superconducting order well above Tc. Combined with earlier Hall and magnetoresistance results, these data imply that the overdoped cuprate strange metal contains two transport sectors with distinct particle-hole symmetry: a conventional particle-hole-asymmetric Fermi-liquid (FL) contribution governing the Hall effect and the zero-field thermopower, and a nearly particle-hole-symmetric sector dominating the anomalous longitudinal magnetotransport. We formulate a phenomenological real-space model in which disconnected FL islands are embedded in a compensated Dirac liquid of phase-incoherent d-wave Bogoliubov quasiparticles. This picture reconciles conventional zero-field transport with anomalous magnetothermopower and magnetoresistance and offers a concrete framework for thinking about strange metallicity in overdoped cuprates.
summary: This work investigates strange metallicity in overdoped cuprates by measuring magnetothermopower up to 35 T. The key finding is that the anomalous field dependence cannot be explained by standard theory, suggesting two coexisting charge carrier sectors. The authors propose a model where conventional Fermi-liquid behavior coexists with an unusual, particle-hole symmetric component linked to superconducting fluctuations.
main_problem: The study aims to understand the microscopic origin of 'strange metallicity' observed in overdoped cuprate superconductors by analyzing their transport properties.
main_result: The anomalous magnetothermopower suggests the existence of two distinct charge carrier sectors: a conventional Fermi-liquid sector and a nearly particle-hole symmetric sector dominated by superconducting fluctuations above Tc.
method: The research combines high-field magnetothermopower measurements with theoretical modeling using Boltzmann transport theory and phenomenological real-space models.
model_or_system: The physical system is overdoped (Bi,Pb)2(Sr,La)2CuO6+delta single crystals. The model proposes disconnected Fermi-liquid islands embedded in a compensated Dirac liquid of d-wave Bogoliubov quasiparticles.
key_observables: Magnetothermopower $S(H)$, zero-field Seebeck coefficient $S(T)$, Hall resistivity $ho_{xy}(T, H)$, and magnetoresistance (MR).
important_parameters: Magnetic fields up to 35 T; temperature dependence near Tc; doping level in cuprates.
main_assumptions: The model is phenomenological, assuming the coexistence of two distinct transport sectors governed by different symmetries (particle-hole asymmetry).
figures_summary: Figures show $ho_{ab}(T)$ and $S(T)$ vs. doping, detailed characterization of magnetothermopower $|S/T|$ vs. magnetic field, and procedures for symmetrizing the measured thermoelectric voltages.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the failure of standard Boltzmann theory to explain field-dependent thermopower, leading to the hypothesis of multiple transport sectors; it then develops a two-fluid model (FL islands in a Dirac liquid) to reconcile zero-field and high-field anomalies.
why_interesting: While focused on cuprates, the concept of separating transport into distinct symmetry sectors (e.g., particle-hole symmetric vs. asymmetric) is relevant for understanding exotic quantum states in other correlated systems where multiple degrees of freedom coexist.

Figure 3 shows the magnetic-field dependence of the absolute Seebeck coefficient |S/T(H)| for all Bi2201 sam- ples within the temperature range 3.6 K ≤T ≤45 K. A clear transition from a superconducting to a mixed state can be seen for all samples with a Tc > 2 K. All samples exhibit a highly field-dependent |S/T| with a peak struc- ture that becomes more prominent with decreasing T. Notably, the field derivative of the magnetothermopower (MTEP) at 35 T is positive (i. e. d|S/T|/d(µ0H) > 0) at T ∼40 K and becomes negative as T decreases.
